_note: Three demo fact sets written for the demo. Every name, place and event is invented; none is drawn from any evaluation, holdout or court item. Each is written twice (plain and near-statutory wording) because the engine's judges can be sensitive to wording: the live spec runs both. `expect.outcomes` stays null until a fixture has been run at least 3 times in one window and the outcomes recorded on pravrudhi-app#18; the spec's outcome assertion turns strict only then (expect.recorded_runs >= 3).

fixtures.label: PROOF-capable: a dishonest inducement to hand over money on a false claim of authority (cheating, validated contract ipc415_property)

plain: Kavita runs a small shop. In June, Rohan told her he was an authorised wholesale dealer in cloth and offered her forty bales at a discount if she paid in advance.
Rohan knew he had no stock and no authority to sell cloth; in May he had written to a friend that he would take advance payments and not deliver anything.
Because of what Rohan said, Kavita paid him Rs 60,000 in cash and got a signed receipt; no cloth was ever delivered.
formal: The complainant, Kavita, carries on a retail business. In June the accused, Rohan, represented to the complainant that he was an authorised wholesale dealer in cloth and offered forty bales on payment of an advance.
The accused knew at the time that he held no stock and had no authority to sell; in a message to a third person in May he had recorded that he intended to take advances and not to deliver.
Induced by that representation, the complainant delivered Rs 60,000 to the accused as an advance, and no goods were delivered.

fixtures.label: ABSTAIN: facts that do not show the required conditions (validated contract bns85)

plain: Nisha and Karan married in 2019 and live in Pune with his parents.
Nisha works as an engineer. Karan's mother cooks for the household and Nisha helps in the evenings.
The two families meet at festivals and have never had a complaint against each other.
formal: The complainant, Nisha, and the accused, Karan, were married in 2019 and reside at Pune in the household of the accused's parents.
The complainant is employed as an engineer. The household's meals are prepared by the accused's mother, with the complainant assisting in the evenings.
The families of the parties meet on festive occasions, and no complaint of any kind has been made by either against the other.

fixtures.label: REFER: a contract that is not validated is always referred (bns316_misappropriation)

plain: Ravi gave his neighbour Sunil a laptop to keep safe while he travelled for a month.
While Ravi was away, Sunil sold the laptop online and spent the money on himself.
When Ravi returned and asked for it, Sunil said he had lost it.
formal: The complainant, Ravi, entrusted a laptop computer to the accused, Sunil, for safe keeping during the complainant's absence of one month.
During that absence the accused sold the laptop through an online platform and applied the proceeds to his own use.
On the complainant's return and demand for the laptop, the accused stated that it had been lost.
